options.name: action
options.description: Specifies the action for the firewall rule. When C(accept), allows packets with the specified source, destination, and protocol to pass through the firewall. Packets that match the rule and are accepted, traverse the system as if the firewall is not present. When C(drop), drops packets with the specified source, destination, and protocol. options.name: destination
options.description: Specifies packet destinations to which the rule applies. Leaving this field blank applies the rule to all addresses and all ports. You can specify the following destination items. An IPv4 or IPv6 address, an IPv4 or IPv6 address range, geographic location, VLAN, address list, port, port range, port list or address list. You can specify a mix of different types of items for the source address. A special value C(any) can be specified to the destination items to match any value for the respective i

options.name: icmp_message
options.description: Specifies the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) or ICMPv6 message C(type) and C(code) the rule uses. This parameter is only relevant when C(protocol) is either C(icmp)(1) or C(icmpv6)(58).

options.name: irule
options.description: Specifies an iRule that is applied to the firewall rule. An iRule can be started when the firewall rule matches traffic.

options.name: logging
options.description: Specifies whether logging is enabled or disabled for the firewall rule. When creating a new rule, if this parameter is not specified, the default if C(false).

options.name: name
options.description: Specifies the name of the rule.

options.name: parent_policy
options.description: The policy which contains the rule to be managed. One of either C(parent_policy) or C(parent_rule_list) is required.

options.name: parent_rule_list
options.description: The rule list which contains the rule to be managed. One of either C(parent_policy) or C(parent_rule_list) is required.

options.name: partition
options.description: Device partition to manage resources on.

options.name: protocol
options.description: Specifies the protocol to which the rule applies. Protocols may be specified by either their name or numeric value. A special protocol value C(any) can be specified to match any protocol. The numeric equivalent of this protocol is C(255).

options.name: provider
options.description: A dict object containing connection details.

options.name: rule_list
options.description: Specifies an existing rule list to use in the rule. This parameter is mutually exclusive with many of the other individual-rule specific settings. This includes C(logging), C(action), C(source), C(destination), C(irule'), C(protocol) and C(logging). This parameter is only used when C(parent_policy) is specified, otherwise it is ignored.

options.name: schedule
options.description: Specifies a schedule for the firewall rule. You configure schedules to define days and times when the firewall rule is made active.

options.name: source
options.description: Specifies packet sources to which the rule applies. Leaving this field blank applies the rule to all addresses and all ports. You can specify the following source items. An IPv4 or IPv6 address, an IPv4 or IPv6 address range, geographic location, VLAN, address list, port, port range, port list or address list. You can specify a mix of different types of items for the source address. A special value C(any) can be specified to all the source items to match any value for the respective item.

options.name: state
options.description: When C(state) is C(present), ensures the rule exists. When C(state) is C(absent), ensures the rule is removed.

options.name: status
options.description: Indicates the activity state of the rule or rule list. When C(disabled), specifies the rule or rule list does not apply at all. When C(enabled), specifies the system applies the firewall rule or rule list to the given context and addresses. When C(scheduled), specifies the system applies the rule or rule list according to the specified schedule. When creating a new rule, if this parameter is not provided, the default is C(enabled).
